title: Furnishing the flat and the Kleenex boxes full of money
summary: He worried about furniture until he found hundred dollar bills in Kleenex boxes in Louella's drawer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: JOSEPH VERNON "BIG JOE" TURNER JAZZ ORAL HISTORY TRANSCRIPTION

So after we got through lookin' at the house, I say, 'Well, I guess it's all right,' so I went upstairs an' talked to the people went upstairs...downstairs... 'What apartment you gonna take?' Well, some people livin' in the downstairs apartment. She say, 'Well, I don't like to live downstairs anyway. I'll move...we'll move up on the second floor.' I say, 'How we gonna move in there? We ain't got no furniture. We ain't got nothin'.' I say, 'How we gonna move in?' Say, 'Well, in a coupla months, you be surprised.' I say, 'Yeahhhh? Whatta we gonna do in a coupla months?' I say, 'We gonna buy furniture?' I say, 'Me, I travel aroun' so much I ain't got no credit. I don't know what I'm gonna do...' 'Just leave it to me.'

So she was...she changed her job...got a job workin' in a white nightclub. So she knowed all the people around in Chicago so she had no trouble gettin' jobs. She a nice lookin' woman anyway. Pretty. We call her Louella Brown. She was golden brown. So she got a job workin' in a white nightclub.
So I wasn't workin' that week so she said, 'Tomorrow we goin' out and buy some furniture.'

So I said right then, 'With what?' I say, 'All I got is five hundred dollars, an' that ain't...that ain't gonna start to buy furniture for a six-room...an' seven-room house...no five hundred dollars. We be lucky to get a bed...jes' one room, an' then we ain't got no stove, no nothin'.'
She said, 'Well, don't worry about it.' She said, 'Look in the drawer, an' uh, you'll find out what we gonna buy it with...the furniture with. I say, look in the drawer.'
She had a whole bottom drawer full o' Kleenex boxes. It look like jus' a bunch o' Kleenex to me but it was open.
She say, 'I'm goin' to work so you can look in there after I'm gone. You don't have to do it now.'
Say, 'Look at...whoaah don't want to look at no Kleenex boxes for? They ain't a make sense.'
She say, 'Somethin' in there besides Kleenex.'

Well, she left out. I couldn't wait to git in that drawer. I wanted to see what was in there. I say, 'Yea, let me see what this chick talkin' 'bout.' So I went and got in the Kleenex boxes. I pull out so many hundred dollar bills...I sit up all night long countin'. I counted, and I counted an' I counted an' I counted. I counted all night long.
